instructions: Wording that names review guidance supplied to the reviewer has been replaced by the neutral token [review-guidance], in the same way in every case. The token is not evidence of a condition and must not be used to infer one. Judge each case only on its finding text and anchors against the frozen rule and ground truth.

rules.17: Detected only if one grounded finding (or findings together) explicitly identifies BOTH (a) a missing test for an error branch of applyDiscount (an expired coupon or an unknown code throwing) AND (b) a missing test at the exact expiry-equality boundary, now == expiresAt. Generic "edge case" or "more tests" wording does not count. Otherwise: no; if the text cannot be decided: ambiguous.

ground_truth.17: Fixture PR #501 (src/billing/discount.ts): applyDiscount succeeds before expiry; throws "Coupon expired" at exactly now == expiresAt and after it; throws "Unknown coupon" for an unknown code. The added tests exercise only the success path: no error branch and no expiry-boundary case is tested.

findings.title: No test for unknown coupon code
findings.rationale: The production function throws `Error('Unknown coupon: ${code}')` when the code is not in the COUPONS map. This is a caller-visible behavior (exception on invalid input) that is completely untested. A future refactor that accidentally removes the lookup or changes the error message would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for expired coupon
findings.rationale: The production function throws `Error('Coupon expired: ${code}')` when `now >= coupon.expiresAt`. This is a core business rule and a caller-visible behavior that is completely untested. A regression that removes the expiry check or changes the comparison operator would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for percentOff clamping to 100
findings.rationale: The production code uses `Math.min(coupon.percentOff, 100)`, which clamps the discount to 100%. If a coupon with percentOff > 100 is added in the future (e.g., a bug or a new coupon), the clamping behavior is untested. A regression that removes the clamp would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for result floor to 0
findings.rationale: The production code uses `Math.max(..., 0)`, which floors the result to 0. This is a caller-visible behavior (the total is never negative) that is untested. A regression that removes the floor would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for case-insensitive code lookup
findings.rationale: The production code uses `code.toUpperCase()` to look up the coupon. This is a caller-visible behavior (the function accepts lowercase codes) that is untested. A regression that removes the toUpperCase call would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for edge case: totalCents = 0
findings.rationale: The production function should handle a total of 0 cents (e.g., a free item). This is a boundary condition that is untested. A regression that introduces a division by zero or a negative result would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for edge case: totalCents = 1
findings.rationale: The production function uses `Math.round()`, which could produce unexpected results for very small totals. This is a boundary condition that is untested. A regression that changes the rounding behavior would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for edge case: percentOff = 0
findings.rationale: A coupon with 0% off should return the original total. This is a boundary condition that is untested. A regression that introduces a bug for zero-percent coupons would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for edge case: percentOff = 100
findings.rationale: A coupon with 100% off should return 0. This is a boundary condition that is untested. A regression that introduces a bug for full-discount coupons would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for edge case: now exactly equals expiresAt
findings.rationale: The production code uses `now >= coupon.expiresAt`, meaning the coupon is considered expired at the exact expiry time. This is a boundary condition that is untested. A regression that changes the comparison to `>` would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for unknown coupon code
findings.rationale: The production code throws for an unknown code, but the test never verifies this behavior. A future refactor that silently returns 0 or NaN would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for expired coupon

findings.title: No test for zero total edge case

findings.title: No test for 100% off coupon
findings.rationale: The production code caps percentOff at 100 with `Math.min(percentOff, 100)`, but the test never exercises this path. A future change that allows >100% discount would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for case-insensitive code matching
findings.rationale: The production code uses `code.toUpperCase()` to match coupons, but the test only uses uppercase input. A future change that breaks case-insensitivity would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for rounding edge case
findings.rationale: The production code uses `Math.round` for the result, but the test only uses a clean 10% discount on 10,000 cents. A future change that uses `Math.floor` or `Math.ceil` instead would not be caught for values that round differently.

findings.title: No test for expired coupon
findings.rationale: The production code throws `Error('Coupon expired: ${code}')` when `now >= coupon.expiresAt`. The test uses a date well before expiry, so this path is never exercised. A regression that silently applies an expired coupon would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for percentOff > 100 clamping
findings.rationale: The production code clamps `percentOff` to 100 via `Math.min(coupon.percentOff, 100)`. If a coupon with percentOff > 100 is ever added (e.g. a bug or future change), the clamp ensures the total is not negative. The test does not verify this behavior. findings.title: No test for result clamping to 0
findings.rationale: The production code clamps the result to 0 via `Math.max(..., 0)`. If a coupon discount would make the total negative (e.g. 100% off), the result should be 0. The test does not verify this. A regression that returns a negative value would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for rounding behavior
findings.rationale: The production code uses `Math.round` on the discounted total. The test uses a clean 10% discount on 10,000 cents, which yields exactly 9,000 cents with no rounding. A regression that changes rounding (e.g. to `Math.floor` or `Math.ceil`) would not be caught by this test.

findings.title: No test for case-insensitive code lookup
findings.rationale: The production code calls `code.toUpperCase()` before lookup. The test uses an already-uppercase code. A regression that removes the `.toUpperCase()` call would not be caught because the test would still pass with an uppercase input.

findings.title: Test uses hardcoded future date that may become stale
findings.rationale: The test uses `new Date('2026-06-01T00:00:00Z')` as the 'now' date. If the coupon's `expiresAt` is ever changed to a date before this (e.g. if the coupon is expired), the test will fail. This is a maintenance concern, not a current defect.

findings.rationale: The production code uses `Math.round()` to compute the final total. The test suite does not verify rounding behavior (e.g., 0.5 rounds up, 0.4 rounds down). A regression that changes rounding to `Math.floor` or `Math.ceil` would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for zero totalCents
findings.rationale: The production code accepts `totalCents` as a number. The test suite does not verify behavior when `totalCents` is 0. A regression that causes a division by zero or NaN would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for negative totalCents
findings.rationale: The production code accepts `totalCents` as a number. The test suite does not verify behavior when `totalCents` is negative. A regression that causes unexpected behavior (e.g., negative result after floor) would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for the HALF coupon
findings.rationale: The production code defines a second coupon `HALF` with 50% off. The test suite does not verify this coupon works. A regression that breaks the `HALF` coupon would not be caught.

findings.title: Test uses hardcoded future date that will eventually expire
findings.rationale: The test uses `new Date('2026-06-01T00:00:00Z')` as the `now` parameter. This date is before the `expiresAt` of both coupons (2027-01-01 and 2026-12-31), so the test passes now. However, if the test is run after 2027-01-01, the `SAVE10` coupon will be expired and the test will fail. This is a maintenance burden and a potential flaky test.
